title: KnowledgeEnvelope
description:
A signed knowledge batch as it travels to `POST /api/v1/knowledge`.

Mirrors [`Envelope`] exactly (same framing, same signing rule): the signature
is computed over the canonical-JSON (RFC 8785) encoding of `payload` only.
Knowledge is a **separate, consent-gated channel** beside attestations — it
never rides [`AttestationBatch`] (decision D-0001), has its own sync cursors,
and flows only when the producer's `[sync] knowledge` knob is enabled AND the
workspace has opted in cloud-side.

deviceId.description: ULID of the device that produced and signed this batch.

payload.description: The knowledge batch being attested to.

BodyRef.description:
A requirement or task id with its markdown text — CONTENT (consent-gated),
only ever inside the allowlisted [`SpecSource`] full-tier fields.

KnowledgeBatch.description:
The unit of knowledge sync: zavet decisions, specs, trailer refs, guard
events, and per-repo coverage stats captured locally.

Idempotent by `batchId` (deterministic over the covered items + tier, so a
crash-retry re-sends identical bytes) and by per-item natural keys cloud-side
— wipe-and-resync reproduces cloud state.

**Tiering.** At `tier: "metadata"` (the default when the channel is enabled
at all) every content field — `bodyMd` on decisions and specs, `value` on
trailer refs — is `None`/absent: ids, slugs, titles, status, globs, shas,
trailer keys + decision refs, and counts are enough for dashboards to show
structure, cost, and guard telemetry without any prose. `tier: "full"`
populates them, and only a workspace that separately opted in stores them.
[`KnowledgeBatch::strip_content`] is the producer-side downgrade.

batchId.description: Deterministic idempotency key for this batch (content-derived, not a ULID).

deviceId.description: ULID of the producing device (matches the envelope).

generatedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp the batch was assembled.

tier.description:
`"metadata"` or `"full"` — what the batch was built under. A string, not
an enum, so new tiers are additive without a schema major bump. The cloud
gates on the actual content fields too, never on this label alone.

KnowledgeCheck.description:
One verification binding on a decision or spec.

The split is deliberate, and follows D-0001's rule that content needs its
own opt-in. A `label` names an invariant the way a `title` names a record —
metadata. A `command` is a line of the repo's own build configuration: it
can name internal tooling, hosts and paths nobody agreed to publish by
turning knowledge sync on. So the label rides at every tier and the command
is consent-gated exactly like `bodyMd`.

An unlabeled check has `label == command` at the source, so the metadata
tier degrades to a label that reads like a command. That is not a leak: it
is the name its author chose, in the same position `title` already
occupies.

command.description:
CONTENT (consent-gated): the command that verifies it. `None` unless
the batch is full-tier. Allowlisted in the no-content-fields invariant.

label.description: Human label for the invariant. Metadata.

KnowledgeDecision.description:
One zavet decision record, metadata-first.

`recordSha` is the git blob oid of the record file (a content-identity
pointer like [`BlobRef::blob`], never the file's bytes). `bodyMd` is the
consent-gated content field — `None` at the metadata tier.

bodyMd.description:
CONTENT (consent-gated): the record body markdown. `None` unless the
batch is full-tier. Allowlisted in the no-content-fields invariant.

checks.description:
How this record's invariants are verified — see [`KnowledgeCheck`] for
why only half of a check crosses at the metadata tier.

correctedBy.description:
A later decision that corrects one claim in this one. The record stays
`active` — this is lineage, like `supersedes`, not a status.

createdAt.description: Author date of the introducing commit, RFC 3339.

firstCommit.description: Commit that first introduced the record (first-sight provenance).

lastCommit.description: Most recent commit that touched the record.

origin.description: How the record came to be: `recorded` | `reverse-engineered` | …

path.description: Repo-relative path of the record file.

recordSha.description: Git blob oid of the record file (identity pointer, not content).

sourceSession.description: The session attributed to the introducing commit, if uniquely known.

supersedes.description: The decision this one supersedes, if any.

title.description: Human title — metadata (it names the record, like a filename).

updatedAt.description: Author date of the latest touching commit, RFC 3339.

verified.description: True only after a human confirmed the record matches reality.

KnowledgeGuardEvent.description:
One guard event (shown / blocked / complied / overridden / superseded) —
pure telemetry, always metadata.

id.description: ULID (the idempotency key for this event).

kind.description:
Event kind — stored verbatim (a plugin newer than the daemon degrades
to "recorded, filtered at query time").

sessionId.description: The attributed session, if uniquely known.

KnowledgeRepoStats.description:
Per-repo knowledge coverage/capture snapshot, computed producer-side (only
the daemon can walk git history and match paths against guard/spec globs).
Counts only — feeds the dashboard's "Knowledge coverage" and "Capture
ratio" tiles. Upserted per repo cloud-side (a snapshot, not a stream).

activePaths.description: Distinct paths touched by commits inside the window.

computedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp the snapshot was computed.

coveredPaths.description:
Of those, paths covered by an active guard glob or any captured spec
(every spec contributes its globs, verified or not — D-0017).

nontrivialCommits.description: Non-merge commits in the window touching non-`.zavet/` paths.

specCitedCommits.description:
Of `nontrivial_commits`, those citing any captured spec slug in a
`Spec:` trailer. Sits next to `trailer_commits`.

specSources.description:
Spec frameworks declared via `spec-source:` in `.zavet/config`, with
unit counts by normalised state. Metadata (kinds, roots, counts).

trailerCommits.description: Of those, commits carrying at least one knowledge trailer.

windowDays.description:
The **effective** rolling window the counts cover, in days.

Capped at 90, but clamped down to the days since the repo adopted
`.zavet/`: counting commits from before the practice existed as "missed
capture" made the ratios read far too low on repos with long history
(issue #67). Consumers should render this value rather than assume 90.

zavetSince.description:
RFC 3339 author date of the commit that added `.zavet/` — when the repo
adopted the practice these counts measure. `None` when it can't be dated.

Lets a consumer say *why* `window_days` is short ("coverage over the 34
days since zavet started") instead of a bare number that reads like a bug.
Optional and skipped when absent so older payloads stay byte-identical.

KnowledgeSpec.description: One living spec, metadata-first. Same tiering rules as [`KnowledgeDecision`].

bodyMd.description:
CONTENT (consent-gated): the spec body markdown. `None` unless the
batch is full-tier. Allowlisted in the no-content-fields invariant.

checks.description:
Feature-level scenarios proving this spec's behavior still holds. Same
label/command tiering as a decision's — see [`KnowledgeCheck`].

decisions.description: Linked decision ids (frontmatter ∪ body refs, canonical, deduplicated).

path.description: Repo-relative path of the spec file.

paths.description: Git pathspecs the spec covers (staleness surface).

recordSha.description: Git blob oid of the spec file (identity pointer, not content).

source.description:
Set only for source-backed units (OpenSpec, Spec Kit, BMAD,
superpowers) — see [`SpecSource`]. `path` then holds the unit's primary
document and `first_commit`/`last_commit`/`created_at`/`updated_at`
carry the unit's git history. Absent for native zavet specs.

verified.description: True only after a human confirmed spec-matches-code.

KnowledgeTrailerRef.description:
One commit trailer occurrence: the key and the decision it references.

The trailer's free-text `value` is CONTENT (author prose, like a commit
message) — `None` at the metadata tier; keys + refs alone already draw the
decision↔commit graph.

decisionId.description: First canonical `D-NNNN` referenced by the value, if any.

seq.description: Position of this trailer within the commit's trailer block.

specRefs.description:
For a `spec` trailer: the comma-split values that EXACTLY match a
captured spec slug. Those slugs already cross as `KnowledgeSpec.slug`,
so this is metadata at every tier and survives
[`KnowledgeBatch::strip_content`] — it is what lets a metadata-tier
workspace join commits to specs (per-spec effort and throughput).
Never free text: a value that is not a known slug is simply absent.

value.description:
CONTENT (consent-gated): the trailer's free text. `None` unless the
batch is full-tier (policy-gated: the token denylist cannot see the
word `value`, so the metadata-tier test pins its absence explicitly).

RepoSpecSource.description: One declared spec-framework source in a repo, with its unit census.

units.description: Number of units found under the root.

RequirementRef.description:
A requirement's id and state. The id (`R1`, `FR-001`) is an identifier; the
requirement text is full-tier only ([`SpecSource::requirement_bodies`]).

SpecCounts.description:
Shape counts of a spec unit. All metadata; zero when the kind has no such
concept.

storyStatus.description: Story counts by status word (BMAD), e.g. `{"done": 3, "ready": 2}`.

SpecDrift.description:
Planned-vs-touched drift counts for a spec unit. No "satisfied" or
"compliant" judgement is ever carried.

SpecGroup.description:
A spec unit's grouping (BMAD initiative / epic, Spec Kit feature number,
OpenSpec capability).

SpecSource.description:
Spec-framework provenance and shape for a source-backed [`KnowledgeSpec`]
(slug `<kind>:<id>`, `origin: external`, never `verified`).

Everything outside the "full tier" block is metadata: identifiers, enums,
counts, timestamps and blob oids — requirement and task *ids* are
identifiers the framework itself prints, not prose. The full-tier block is
consent-gated exactly like `bodyMd`: cleared by
[`KnowledgeBatch::strip_content`] and pinned in the no-content-fields
invariant. Assignees and any personal frontmatter fields never cross.

capabilities.description: OpenSpec capability directory names touched by the unit's deltas.

closedOn.description: The date the unit closed (`2026-09-30`), when the framework records one.

frameworkVersion.description: The framework's own version, when it can be read.

group.description: Initiative / epic / capability / feature grouping, when the kind has one.

id.description: The unit id within its framework, e.g. `add-csv-import`.

nativeState.description: The framework's own state word, verbatim.

plannedPaths.description:
Paths the framework *claims* the unit will touch — a claim, never
coverage (coverage stays in `KnowledgeSpec.paths`).

requirementBodies.description:
CONTENT (consent-gated): requirement text by id. Empty unless the
batch is full-tier. Named `*_bodies`, never `*_body`, so the whole-token
denylist stays meaningful; allowlisted by exact path.

requirementRefs.description: Requirement ids with state — ids only, never the requirement text.

stateChangedAt.description: RFC 3339 instant dira observed `state` change (stamped producer-side).

summaryMd.description:
CONTENT (consent-gated): the unit summary (proposal "Why", Spec Kit
summary, epic description). `None` unless full-tier.

taskBodies.description: CONTENT (consent-gated): task text by id. Empty unless full-tier.

taskRefs.description: Task ids with progress — ids only, never the task text.

trackerRefs.description:
CONTENT (consent-gated): tracker references (`GH#123`, `PROJ-42`) from
framework frontmatter. Empty unless full-tier — they can name private
trackers, so they ride with the content tier.

unitFiles.description: The unit's files with their git blob oids (identity pointers).

TaskRef.description:
A task's id and progress. The task text is full-tier only
([`SpecSource::task_bodies`]).

story.description: The user story the task belongs to (`US1`), when the kind has them.

UnitFile.description: One file of a spec unit, identified by git blob oid (never its bytes).
